sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northwestern residential quarter of Riverside between Fairview on the west and Pavilion Avenue on the east, from Polk down to Adams and the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division along Lafayette Avenue in the southeast corner, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Madison runs diagonally through the middle of the sheet, crossing Polk, Jefferson, Monroe and Adams, which run across the page at a slant. Most of the blocks are filled with frame dwellings, many of two and two-and-a-half storeys, with rear sheds, auto garages and a few stores; several blocks along Polk and Pavilion Avenue hold rows of attached brick houses. Business is concentrated at the southeast corner, where Lafayette Avenue faces the railroad: a row of brick and concrete-block stores and dwellings, the Avenue Hotel at the corner of Pavilion Avenue, Corrigan's Hotel, a public garage for 20 cars and a warehouse. The railroad passenger station, with its waiting room and a concrete platform, lies between the tracks and Lafayette Avenue. In the northeast corner, beyond Polk at Pavilion Avenue, stand the National Compound Company's soap factory, a building used for making iron toys, and a second large garage with auto supplies; this corner is also covered by sheet 8. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The blocks west of Fairview are on sheet 8, and the area south of Adams on sheet 5.
notes: Lafayette Avenue is Lafayette Street in OpenStreetMap; Fairview is Fairview Street.
The Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) is today NJ Transit's River Line.

50 ft. Fairview to Pavilion Av., Polk to Adams and Lafayette Av. (PRR station). Streets Polk, Jefferson, Monroe, Adams, Madison, Fairview, Pavilion Av., Lafayette Av. Top right corner (beyond Polk at Pavilion) repeats the hotel and soap factory of sheet 8 part 2. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the industrial strip of northeastern Riverside along the Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) between Pavilion Avenue on the west and Clay Street on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The railroad tracks cross the sheet diagonally, with Franklin Avenue running beside them. West of the tracks stand the large works of the Keystone Watch Case Company, a long reinforced concrete fireproof building and a group of numbered shops, together with the Riverside Metal Company's melting shops, rolling and wire mills, engine room and foundry, and a long steel rolling mill with a raised ventilator. The Public Service Railways Company car barn and repair shop occupies the top left corner. Many of these buildings are marked with pipe lines, hydrants and a well. East of the tracks the plan shows blocks of frame dwellings, some of them paired or in rows, laid out between Fillmore, Taylor, Kossuth and Bridgeborough Road, all crossed by Clay Street on the right. Notable buildings there include the Riverside Ice and Cold Storage Company, the Homestead boarding house, Zurbrugg Memorial Hospital, a sausage factory, two garages and the Bell Telephone central office. Four- and six-inch water mains run along the streets. The sheet carries a north arrow at the lower right and a scale of feet at the bottom. The cross streets are drawn about 50 feet wide.
notes: Fillmore is spelled Filmore Street in OpenStreetMap.
Bridgeborough Road is today Bridgeboro Street.
The lettering along the left edge reads Pavilion Av.; the Keystone Watch Case Company name is also lettered along it.

50 ft. One part: strip along the PRR between Pavilion Av. and Clay, Keystone Watch Case Co. works at left (no junctions there); control from Clay, Fillmore, Taylor, Kossuth, Bridgeborough Rd, Franklin Av. (all on the east side).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the blocks of northeastern Riverside between Clay Street on the west and Washington Street on the east, from Harrison Street in the north down to Bridgeborough Road in the south, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Hecker Street runs through the middle of the sheet, crossing Bem, Fillmore, Taylor and Kossuth Streets, which are drawn as parallel cross streets. The northern part, beyond Harrison Street and around Bem Street, is still largely open land divided into large numbered blocks with only a few dwellings. South of Fillmore Street the blocks are built up with rows of frame dwellings, many of them two-family or paired houses, with sheds and auto garages at the rear of the lots. Industry is concentrated near Clay Street: the Henry Taubel and Son Hosiery Mill occupies a large brick group at the corner of Clay and Kossuth Streets, and William Holt and Son's paper box manufactory stands beside it on Taylor Street. The Krug and Roan Hosiery Mill stands on Fillmore Street east of Hecker, John Blaufuss's bottling works on Taylor Street, and the Oberg, Fell and Fisher ice company on the west side of Hecker. The I.O.M. Hall, a public hall with a lodge room, stands on Taylor Street east of Hecker. Water pipes of 2 to 8 inches are marked along Fillmore Street and Bridgeborough Road, with fire hydrants and a fire alarm box. The bottom margin carries the scale of feet and the lettered ends of Scott, Hancock and Webster Streets, which continue on sheet 7.
notes: Fillmore is spelled Filmore Street in OpenStreetMap.
Bridgeborough Road is today Bridgeboro Street.
Washington along the east edge is East Washington Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Clay to Washington, Harrison to Bridgeborough Rd; Hecker, Bem, Fillmore, Taylor, Kossuth. Taubel hosiery mill, Holt paper box. Pilot sheet. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the central industrial part of Riverside between Adams Street at the top and the Zion Lutheran church block near the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right, with Lafayette Avenue on its north side and New Jersey Avenue on its south side, and a freight depot, passenger station, plank platform, express office and baggage house stand along the line at the upper right. North of the railroad, between Fairview and Madison Streets, are rows of frame dwellings, a coal yard and a wagon shed, and further left a garage and a lumber storage yard. South of the tracks the sheet is dominated by the large pink brick and fireproof buildings of the Wm. F. Taubel hosiery mills, numbered 1 to 16, with dye houses, bleach house, store house, wooden water tanks and sprinkler equipment, between New Jersey Avenue, Fairview Street and Delaware Avenue. East of Fairview Street are the Riverside Milling and Coal Company's flour mill and storage, a garage, the Riverside Turngemeinde club, the American Legion hall and a block of stores along Pavilion Avenue. West Scott and West Hancock Streets run across the right half, and the Pavilion Hotel stands on Pavilion Avenue at the lower right. A heavy V-shaped line near the bottom encloses the Zion Lutheran Church block, beyond which the blocks marked 9 and 11 belong to other sheets. A block of text on the sprinkler and fire protection of the mills is printed at the lower left, with the scale of feet and a north arrow.
notes: Fairview is Fairview Street in OpenStreetMap; the Fairview junctions fit the modern line only to about 2 to 4 m.
Lafayette Avenue is today Lafayette Street.
West Scott and West Hancock are West Scott Street and West Hancock Street in OpenStreetMap.
Spring Garden (Cass St.) is printed at the lower right edge.

50 ft. One part, Fairview to Pavilion Av. south of the PRR (New Jersey Av., Lafayette Av., W. Scott, W. Hancock, Delaware Av., 2nd St.); Taubel hosiery mills, Riverside Milling and Coal Co. Mask cut around the note table at lower left and the heavy V at the bottom (Zion Lutheran church block drawn here; areas labelled 9 and 11 belong to those sheets). Fairview junctions 2 to 4 m off; medium confidence.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 is the downtown of Riverside, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, between Pavilion Avenue on the west and Middleton Street on the east. Scott, Hancock, Webster and Spring Garden Streets run across the sheet as parallel east-west streets, crossed by Carroll Street in the middle, and Bridgeborough Road cuts diagonally across the top right. The two blocks facing Scott Street and Hancock Street hold the commercial core: the Riverside Trust Company bank on the corner of Pavilion Avenue, a lodge room, shops, the Riverside Auditorium for motion pictures, a printing works, a garage and repair shop, a pool room, and Fire Department Station No. 1 on the north side of Scott Street. The Post Office stands on Pavilion Avenue south of Hancock Street and the Fox Theatre, a large motion picture house with stage and scenery rooms, stands further south on the same avenue. East of Carroll Street the blocks between Hancock, Webster and Spring Garden Streets are almost wholly frame dwellings with small outbuildings, poultry houses and a few sheds. At the top of the sheet the Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) tracks and Franklin Avenue appear in the upper left, with a site marked for a garage. Four-, six-, eight- and twelve-inch water mains run along the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Neighbouring sheets are indicated by the numbers 3, 5 and 7 beyond the edges, and a scale of feet and north arrow are printed on the sheet.
notes: Bridgeborough Road is today Bridgeboro Street.
Spring Garden is printed with (Cass) after it.
Scott, Hancock and Webster are East Scott Street, East Hancock Street and Webster Street in OpenStreetMap; Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street.

50 ft (fitted 8.00 px/ft, 1.5 percent above sheet 4). One part, downtown between Pavilion Av. and Middleton: Scott, Hancock, Webster, Spring Garden (Cass), Bridgeborough Rd, Franklin Av.; blank sheet-5 area west of Pavilion cut out of the mask.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7 covers central Riverside east of Middleton Street, from Scott Street in the north to Paine Avenue in the south, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Bridgeborough Road crosses the upper half of the sheet diagonally from the northwest toward the southeast, and Washington Street runs diagonally across the lower right, meeting Bridgeborough Road near the east edge; a short stretch of Hecker Street leaves Bridgeborough Road toward the north. Between them run the parallel cross streets Hancock, Webster and Spring Garden, the last also lettered with its former name Cass. The north corner holds the church group of St. Peter's Roman Catholic parish: the church on Scott Street and St. Peter's Parochial School on Hancock Street. James Kenney's greenhouses, with glass roofs and a heating plant, fill part of the block south of Hancock Street, and St. Stephen's Memorial Church (Episcopal) and its parish building stand on Bridgeborough Road. The New Central Hotel is at the corner of Middleton and Hancock Streets, and a milk depot and dairy stand on Webster Street. The blocks between Webster Street and Paine Avenue are built up with frame dwellings, many of them two-and-a-half storeys, with rear sheds and garages; the Riverside M.E. Church stands on Spring Garden Street near Washington Street. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Much of the area east of Washington Street is left blank and belongs to sheet 12; the National Lock Washer Company works in the upper right corner is a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Spring Garden is printed with its old name Cass in parentheses; today Spring Garden Street.
Bridgeborough Road is today Bridgeboro Street; Washington is East Washington Street; Paine Avenue is Paine Street; Scott and Hancock are East Scott and East Hancock Streets in OpenStreetMap.

50 ft. Part 1: Middleton to Washington/Bridgeborough Rd, Scott to Paine Av. (St. Peter's R.C., Kenney greenhouses). Part 2: inset of the National Lock Washer Co. on New Jersey Av., "located 1 mile from Riverside R.R. Sta." (west, in Delran); no street junction, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The National Lock Washer Co. works on New Jersey Avenue, about 1 mile west of Riverside station (no street junction; only New Jersey Avenue and the railroad are drawn; needs hand-picked control from the plant site (modern building or parcel corners) along New Jersey Avenue in Delran).

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 8 is the western half of the page: a narrow strip of the northwestern edge of Riverside lying west of Fairview, between Polk in the north and Adams in the south, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Polk, Jefferson, Monroe and Adams run across the strip from Fairview toward the west and end within it; an unnamed lane runs north and south through the middle of the blocks. The area was thinly built in 1925. Block 259 north of Polk is open land, and blocks 258, 257 and 31 hold scattered frame dwellings with sheds and garages, most of them fronting on Fairview, with a storage shed near Jefferson. The Public Service sub-station, a small brick building, stands on Fairview between Jefferson and Monroe. Water pipes of 4 inches are marked in Fairview, with a fire hydrant at Jefferson and another near Adams. The west margin is lettered "No exposure". The blocks east of Fairview are drawn on sheet 2, and a heavy line divides this part from part 2 of the sheet, the lumber yard on Pavilion Avenue by Rancocas Creek.
notes: Fairview is Fairview Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed by a helmert fit on four junctions along Fairview only; Polk and Jefferson are today continued west to American Legion Drive.

50 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1 (west half): west of Fairview, Polk to Adams (helmert on Fairview junctions). Part 2 (east half): Pavilion Av. from north of Polk to Rancocas Creek, J. S. Collins & Son lumber yard; no junction, placed from building corners carried from sheet 2 plus a derived point along Pavilion Av.

sheet-8-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 8 is the eastern half of the page, separated from part 1 by a heavy line. It shows the west side of Pavilion Avenue from just north of Polk Street up to the south bank of Rancocas Creek, where the avenue bends to the northeast and crosses the creek by the bridge to Delanco, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Almost the whole part is taken up by the yard of J. S. Collins and Son, dealers in lumber, farm supplies and hardware and builders: long lumber sheds and lumber and roofing storage along Pavilion Avenue, hardwood lumber storage, a lime shed and lime tank, hardware storage, an office with scales, a wagon shed, hay storage and a two-storey tile building for offices, hardware, cement and hay storage with lumber mill work above. A small electrically driven saw mill stands near the creek, and open lumber piles are drawn in outline along the shore. At the south end of the part are a hotel and the north end of a factory building fronting on Pavilion Avenue, both also drawn on sheet 2, and on the east side of the avenue the Public Service lamp houses. Water pipes of 8 and 12 inches run along Pavilion Avenue. The rest of block 107 west of the yard is open land.
notes: No street junction is drawn on this part. It was placed from four building corners carried from sheet 2 and one point derived along Pavilion Avenue at sheet 2's scale and rotation.

Check: the drawn bridge end falls about 12 m north of the south end of the modern Pavilion Avenue bridge in OpenStreetMap; the drawn bend of Pavilion Avenue agrees with the modern bend within a few metres.

50 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1 (west half): west of Fairview, Polk to Adams (helmert on Fairview junctions). Part 2 (east half): Pavilion Av. from north of Polk to Rancocas Creek, J. S. Collins & Son lumber yard; no junction, placed from building corners carried from sheet 2 plus a derived point along Pavilion Av.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 is the western residential district of Riverside, drawn at 100 feet to an inch (a scale line is printed on the sheet). The New Jersey Avenue railroad line (Pennsylvania Railroad, Amboy Division) runs north to south down the left side, with a wide block of open land to its west that is mostly blank, carrying only a printing works, a lumber storage building, a garage and a few sheds. East of the tracks the built-up blocks form a regular grid between Fairview at the top and Rancocas and Chester Avenues at the bottom. Delaware, Cleveland, Heulings, Lippincott and Rancocas Avenues run across the sheet, crossed by 2nd Street and 3rd Street, with a column of blocks on each side of 2nd Street. The blocks are lined with frame dwellings, mostly two-storey detached houses with a few brick and concrete ones, set on narrow deep lots with small outbuildings. The Catholic Church of Riverside and its rectory stand in block 207 on the south side of Lippincott Avenue, west of 2nd Street. The northern blocks near Fairview and the blocks marked 5 belong to sheet 5, and the blocks marked 10 and 14 beyond the edges belong to neighbouring sheets. A compass rose is drawn in the upper middle and Pavilion Avenue and Rush Street appear at the top right corner. Water mains of four and six inches run in most streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The south edge shows Chester Avenue and the head of Roland Street at the lower left.
notes: Fairview is Fairview Street in OpenStreetMap.
The printed scale line reads 100 Ft. to One Inch.
Roland Street is Roland Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

100 ft. One part, west of Fairview along New Jersey Av. (PRR): Delaware, Cleveland, Heulings, Lippincott, Rancocas and Chester Avs., 2nd and 3rd Sts.; west half mostly open land. Rotation about -57 deg.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 is the southwestern residential part of Riverside, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and continuing sheet 9 to the east. The blocks are laid out in a regular grid between Fairview at the top and Chester Avenue at the bottom, with Delaware, Cleveland, Heulings, Lippincott and Rancocas Avenues running across the sheet and 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets running down it. The northern blocks, from Fairview to Cleveland Avenue, are filled with frame dwellings, many of them paired houses, with a few brick and concrete buildings and small outbuildings at the rear of deep lots. Further south the blocks thin out quickly: blocks 215, 218, 219, 220, 221 and 222 are nearly empty land with only isolated dwellings, and the bottom row of blocks 304, 305 and 314 is entirely open. In the lower right the Riverton A. A. Grounds are marked with a small building. Along the right edge Washington Street runs diagonally from the upper right corner past the northeast blocks, and Arnot Street branches off it; the northeast corner is drawn with angled blocks and a stone building. Water mains of four and six inches run in the streets. The street grid is turned on the page, and a compass rose in the upper right shows north pointing up and to the left. Blocks marked 9 at the left and 11 above the sheet and at the right belong to neighbouring sheets. The bottom margin carries the scale of feet and a no exposure note for the last blocks.
notes: Fairview is Fairview Street in OpenStreetMap.
Arnot Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Washington along the right edge is East Washington Street in OpenStreetMap.
Rush Street is printed at the upper left corner.
100 ft. One part, southwest: 3rd to 5th Sts. between Fairview and Chester Av.; Washington and Arnot St. at the right not used for control (Arnot not in OSM).

sheet-11-1.description: The main part of sheet 11 covers the southern part of Riverside at the smaller scale of 100 feet to an inch, from Spring Garden and Rush Streets in the north down to Hooker and 7th Streets in the south. Fairview runs diagonally down the middle of the part from Third Street to Hooker; east of it lie Carroll, Morton, Lee, Middleton and Paine Avenue in the north, Washington across the middle, and Weeks Avenue, Park Avenue, Grant and Rein Avenue in the southeast. West of Fairview the grid of Cleveland Avenue, Delaware Avenue and Arndt Avenue is crossed by 6th and 7th Streets. The north end holds the Riverside Public School, a large brick building on Spring Garden Street, and an open tract lettered Park between Spring Garden Street and Morton. Riverside High School, a brick building with an auditorium, stands in block 234 east of Washington. The Kessey Co. branch kilting mill, not in operation, stands at Delaware Avenue and 6th Street. Elsewhere the blocks hold frame dwellings, many of them small, with sheds and garages; large tracts in the southeast (blocks 213 1/2, 310, 311) and around Weeks Avenue are laid out in narrow building lots with few houses. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are marked in the principal streets. The upper left corner of the page is a separate inset of the blocks along Fairview south of Hooker (part 2), divided from this part by a heavy line.
notes: Spring Garden is printed with its old name Cass in parentheses.
Washington is East Washington Street in OpenStreetMap; Paine Avenue is Paine Street; Third and Fourth Streets are 3rd and 4th Streets.
Rein Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
The junctions of Washington with Lee and with Middleton are one drawn junction; OpenStreetMap has two nodes 6 m apart, and only Lee was used.
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; fitted with a second-order polynomial on 28 junctions.

100 ft ("entire sheet"). Part 1: main map, Spring Garden/Rush to Hooker and 7th St, Cleveland Av. to Rein Av. Part 2: inset in upper left corner (heavy line), Fairview south of Hooker: Sylvan, Progress, Whittaker, Prosper Avs.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is an inset in the upper left corner of the page, set off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, turned about 45 degrees from the page. It shows the southern end of Riverside along Fairview south of Hooker: Sylvan Avenue, Progress Avenue and Whittaker Avenue run east from Fairview to Prosper Avenue, and Weeks Avenue meets Hooker at the top of the inset. Blocks 230, 231, 312 and 313 east of Fairview are laid out in narrow building lots, most of them still vacant in 1925, with a few frame dwellings and garages near Fairview and Whittaker Avenue. West of Fairview, in block 231 1/2, a row of small dwellings fronts on the street. A 6-inch water pipe runs along Fairview. The inset continues the main map southward: its top edge at Hooker meets the bottom of the main part.
notes: Sylvan, Progress and Whittaker Avenues are Sylvan, Progress and Whittaker Streets in OpenStreetMap; Prosper Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
Placed by a helmert fit on four junctions along Fairview only (low confidence).

100 ft ("entire sheet"). Part 1: main map, Spring Garden/Rush to Hooker and 7th St, Cleveland Av. to Rein Av. Part 2: inset in upper left corner (heavy line), Fairview south of Hooker: Sylvan, Progress, Whittaker, Prosper Avs.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the eastern part of Riverside at 100 feet to an inch, from Harrison at the top to Rein Avenue near the bottom, between Washington Street on the west and Layock Street on the east. The blocks at the top, numbered 283 to 293, are largely open land, with a single row of attached houses facing Bem Street in block 286. Dwellings thicken south of Taylor Street: block 103 holds two long rows of attached houses facing Taylor and Kossuth Streets, and the large block between Leach and Burke Streets holds a Cemetery, with a tool house and sheds at its edge. Bridgeborough Road runs east and west across the middle of the sheet lined with detached frame houses, and the Moravian Church stands on it at the corner of Washington Street. A cement block factory is marked at the right in block 292. Below Bridgeborough Road the blocks are only partly built: Howard, Paine and Morton run across blocks 307, 308 and 309, which are nearly empty, while Hooker and Grant run down the middle. At the right Sylvan Avenue and Progress Avenue slant across the sheet, with Butler, Stokes and Pine Streets running into them. Washington Street bends diagonally down the left side, and Webster Street, Spring Garden Street, Paine Avenue and Morton Street are shown running off the left edge into sheet 7. A compass rose is at the upper left, and water mains of four and six inches run along the main streets.
notes: Fillmore is spelled Filmore Street in OpenStreetMap.
Layock is Laycock Street in OpenStreetMap.
Bridgeborough Road is today Bridgeboro Street.
Washington is East Washington Street in OpenStreetMap; Paine Avenue is Paine Street.
Rein Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Paine Avenue jogs about 60 feet at Grant Street on the sheet.

100 ft. One part, east: Washington to Layock, Harrison to Rein Av.; Bem, Fillmore, Taylor, Kossuth, Bridgeborough Rd, Howard, Paine Av., Morton, Leach, Burke, Grant, Hooker, Butler; cemetery. Blank strip at left belongs to sheets 4 and 7.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the far eastern edge of Riverside at 100 feet to an inch, east of sheet 12, from Harrison at the top to Pine at the bottom left. The upper half is a regular grid of blocks numbered 238 to 303, bounded by Layock, Palmer, Dolphin and Henry Streets running north and south and by Harrison, Bem, Fillmore, Taylor and Kossuth Streets running east and west. Most of these blocks are open land with only scattered dwellings, small sheds and a plumber's yard on Palmer Street in block 245; the larger blocks at the left, 295 and 296, hold only a few outbuildings, and the right side of the sheet, block 303 and the open area south of Bridgeborough Road marked 238, is entirely blank. Bridgeborough Road crosses the sheet at about two thirds of the way down, with a loose scatter of houses along it. In the lower left, Progress Avenue and Whittaker Avenue run south past blocks 205 and 237, which hold a few dwellings, to Stokes and Pine Streets, and a compass rose is drawn at the left edge. Fire alarm and hydrant marks are few, and six-inch water mains run along Dolphin Street and Bridgeborough Road. No inset or separately oriented part appears on this sheet. The number 12 at the left edge shows where sheet 12 adjoins, and the scale of feet is printed at the lower right.
notes: Fillmore is spelled Filmore Street in OpenStreetMap.
Layock is Laycock Street in OpenStreetMap.
Bridgeborough Road is today Bridgeboro Street.
Dolphin is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

Palmer Street north of Bridgeborough Road and Whittaker Avenue south of it appear to be one street; OpenStreetMap names them Palmer Street and Whittaker Street with two nodes about 17 m apart at Bridgeboro Street.
100 ft. One part, far east beyond Layock: Harrison to Pine, Palmer, Dolphin, Henry; sparse; no inset. Bridgeboro/Whittaker excluded (OSM node 17 m from Bridgeboro/Palmer at the same drawn junction).

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers Riverside Park, the development west of Riverside proper between the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division and New Jersey Avenue in the south and River Drive along the Delaware River in the north, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Four long avenues run the length of the sheet from New Jersey Avenue toward the river: Norman Avenue, Alden Avenue, Stewart Avenue and Chester Avenue, crossed by Lake, Frederick and Roland. The words Riverside Park are lettered diagonally across the middle of the tract. Almost the whole area is platted in narrow building lots in blocks 269 to 279, most of them still vacant in 1925; frame dwellings, many of one and two storeys with small garages, are scattered along the avenues and grow denser toward New Jersey Avenue and Roland at the south end. Two small ponds, Polz Lake between Alden and Stewart Avenues and Spring Lake west of Chester Avenue, are drawn in blue. The Cambridge Union Mission stands near Roland, and Cambridge Station, a small shelter, is on the railroad at the southwest corner. A narrow strip of the Delaware River shore is shown in the northeast corner beyond River Drive.
notes: Lake, Frederick and Roland are Lake Street, Frederick Avenue and Roland Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Riverside Park lies today in Delran Township, west of the Riverside township line.
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
100 ft. Riverside Park (Delran): Norman, Alden, Stewart, Chester Avs., Lake, Frederick, Roland, New Jersey Av., River Drive; Polz Lake, Spring Lake. One part.
